column2: req_desc

Readiness
GET /api/health answers 200 without a session only once the schema, the seed and the realm accounts are all in place, and 503 with each flag while the desk is still starting, as qualified in API.

One origin
The pages and the JSON API are served by one server on one origin, with the API under the /api prefix.

Production build
The desk is served from a production build whose every route arrives already rendered by the server, never from a development server.

Security headers
Every response carries the content-type, framing and referrer headers stated in Server boundary and no X-Powered-By header.

Real backing services
Every record lives in the postgres database named by DATABASE_URL and every sign-in is checked by the configured identity realm, with no stand-in store.

Seeded people
One employer, Kestrel Works, keeping time in Europe/London, and the sixteen seeded people with their ids, roles, reporting lines, contact details and active flags exist from first start, each work address unique in its folded form.

Seeded attendance and leave
Each person holds the seeded attendance days at their business-time punches with their nine deliberate gaps as rewritten by the seeded approvals, plus the nine seeded annual and sickness leave days, with at most one attendance row and one leave row per person per day.

Seeded corrections and policy
The nine seeded corrections carry ids 1 to 9 in seed-table order, cover all four states and carry their business-time raise and decision instants, and policy version 1 carries the stated defaults.

Seeding runs once
Restarting the desk never duplicates, alters or re-dates a seeded row.

Store invariants
The store holds one pending request per person per day, a decider and decision time on every approved or rejected request and neither on a pending or cancelled one, and a note on every rejected one.

Sign in
A person signs in with a work address and password at /login, lands on the queue scoped to their role or on the safe page they asked for, and sees that role named in the top bar.

One refusal
An unknown work address, a wrong password and a deactivated account with its correct password all receive the identical 401 sign-in refusal stated in Business rules.

Sign out
Signing out ends the session, and its token is refused afterwards with 401 and the signed-out wording.

Identity realm only
Accounts exist only as the seeded people in the identity realm, and no published route creates an account.

Signed-out redirect
A visitor with no valid session to any route in the route table other than /login and /share/<token> is redirected with 303 to /login carrying no record content, with the requested page as next as qualified in Server boundary, and the desk serves no public marketing page.

No credential in the browser
No served page or script carries a service credential, the client secret, an administrative token or a database address.

Employee refusals
An employee gets 403 for changing policy and 404 for reading, deciding or withdrawing another person's request, with the stored state unchanged.

Manager limits
A manager gets 404 for any request that is neither their own nor a current direct report's and 403 for changing policy, with the stored state unchanged.

No self decision
Deciding a request you raised is refused with 403 and the self-decision wording, whatever role you hold.

Administrator never decides
People operations is refused both approve and reject with 403, and the detail screen shows them no decision control.

Unauthenticated calls refused
Every published endpoint except POST /api/session and GET /api/health answers a caller with no valid session with 401 and the signed-out or ended-session wording from API.

Wrong role page
A signed-in person opening a route their role cannot use gets status 403 and the wrong-role wording on that route rather than a redirect.

Scope by relationship
An employee reads only their own requests, a manager only their own and their current direct reports', and people operations every request in the employer.

Scope before filters
A filter value narrows what a caller may see and never widens it, so naming a person outside scope returns no rows.

Queue counts
GET /api/requests returns rows, matched, total, page and pages together, at most twenty five rows a page, and a page beyond the last answers the last page.

Queue order
The default order puts pending first and then the oldest raised first, and sort re-orders by day, raised or person, every order ending in id ascending as stated in Business rules.

Filters and search
The queue narrows by state, correction type, person and month and searches reason text literally and without regard to case, refusing bad values and searches over 100 characters with 400.

Queue beside detail
At the widest tier a person selects a queue row and its request opens in the detail pane on the right while the queue stays on the left, for every role.

Breadcrumb trail
A breadcrumb trail opening at a Desk link sits across the top of every signed-in route and is the navigation.

Queue table
The queue is a table with the eight named columns, captioned {matched} of {total} requests, with tabular figures.

Four empty situations
Nothing raised yet, filters excluding everything, still loading and a failed read each render their own wording from Feedback states, and the failed read offers Try again.

Own not-found page
An unknown request id, a request outside the reader's scope, an unknown shared-link token and an unknown page route answer 404 with the product's own identical not-found page.

Draft row
An employee or manager opens /requests/new, fills the draft row at the head of the queue and sends it, and the new pending request appears in the queue.

Five corrections
Each of the five correction types can be raised with the claimed times its type requires and lands as pending with 201, a night shift ending on the following business day.

Raise checks
A raise is refused in the order published in Business rules, with 400 for a malformed field, 422 for a type switched off, a day outside the window or a claim that contradicts the recorded punches of that day or the days either side, and 409 for a day already pending, creating nothing.

Monthly cap
A raise is refused with 422 once the person's approved and waiting corrections in that month have reached the monthly cap, naming how many of how many are used.

Withdraw
The raiser withdraws a pending request, which frees that day, while anyone else gets 404 or 403 and a request no longer pending gets 409.

Approval writes attendance
Approving writes the claimed business times into that day's attendance record with source regularisation, a night shift's sign-out landing on the following business day.

Rejection note
A rejection needs a note of at least ten characters, stored with the rejected state, and a shorter one is refused with 400.

Decision reply
A decision answers 200 with the request in its new state, including decided_by and decided_at, and an approval needs a note only when policy says so.

Rechecks at approval
An approval re-checks the window and the cap of the policy then in force, counting approved corrections only, and the claim against the attendance as it then stands, so simultaneous approvals for one person never pass the cap or leave overlapping attendance.

Already decided
Of simultaneous decisions on one request exactly one wins, and every later or losing decision gets 409 naming who decided it and when.

Detail evidence
GET /api/requests/<id> returns request, evidence, leave and audit in one read, with the leave kind projected for the reader as in Business rules.

Decide in the browser
A manager approves or rejects from the detail pane and the row shows its new state without a page load, while a refusal other than a 409 leaves the row as it was beside the refusal wording.

Policy versions
People operations changes the policy at /policy through a confirmation naming the next version number, and the new version heads the history with every earlier version still readable.

One type stays enabled
A policy enabling no correction type is refused with 400 and no version is written.

Self approval refused
Setting manager self-approval on is refused with 400 naming self_approval_allowed, and no version records it.

Pending survives tightening
Tightening the policy leaves requests already pending still pending.

Append-only trail
Every decision, policy save, shared-link mint and shared-link revocation appends one attributed audit entry, readable by people operations, that the application's database account cannot update or delete.

Calendar API
GET /api/calendar returns per-day counts and a person lookup computed live only over the caller's current scope, with person matched by work address without regard to case and all-zero days for a person outside it.

Month grid
A manager or people operations reads the month at /calendar with each count beside its own mark shape and a legend showing the same shapes, and narrows it to one person in scope.

Focus-trapping dialogs
The filter sheet and the policy confirmation keep focus inside themselves while open, close on Escape and hand focus back to the control that opened them.

Announcements
Counts and work in progress are announced in a polite region and outcomes and refusals in an assertive one, with the copy from Feedback states.

Landmarks and headings
Every route has banner, main and contentinfo regions, every signed-in route also a navigation region, and each has exactly one first-level heading and no skipped heading levels.

Accessibility audit
The sign-in, queue, raise, detail, calendar, policy and shared-month routes report no serious or critical WCAG 2.2 AA violation at any width tier.

Narrow reflow
No route scrolls sideways at any of the three width tiers.

Own assets
Every icon is inline vector geometry, nothing is requested from another host, and exactly the two named webfont files set the reading and heading families.

Focus ring
Every focusable control shows the same ring, a white separation inside the violet accent, drawn as an outline at least 2 pixels thick rather than as a shadow alone.

Reading tone
Body copy is near-black on a near-white ground.

No idle loops
Nothing on the settled queue animates on a loop.

Reduced motion
Under a reduced-motion preference every motion becomes an instant change of state.

One violet action
The primary action named for each screen is the only thing on that screen wearing the mid, vivid violet.

State as shape, word and tone
Each request state shows as a chip carrying its word, its own glyph and its own tone.

Operational register
The queue reads as a dense operational table whose first 1280x800 screen shows the header band and at least five rows when that many are in scope, with no oversized hero or promotional banner.

Evidence blocks
The detail pane sets what the clock recorded, what is claimed and the leave that day as separately headed blocks, a missing punch reads Not recorded, and the leave block reads the label for the reader's view of its kind.

Draft row in line
The draft row's cells sit under the same column headings as the request rows beneath it.

Narrow tier
On the narrowest tier each queue row becomes a card and the approve and reject pair sticks to the bottom with approve above reject, each spanning the full width.

Every tier keeps every capability
Raising, deciding, filtering, the month view and sharing a month stay reachable at every width tier.

One-transaction decision
The checks, the re-check against the record, the state change, the attendance write and the audit append of a decision land together in one database transaction or not at all.

Delegated identity
Passwords are checked only by the identity realm, and the desk keeps no password or password hash of its own.

Status ladder
Every refusal answers the published status for its kind, from 400 to 429, with a JSON error wording, and the first failing step of the published order decides the answer.

Published fields only
A body field an endpoint does not publish is refused with 400 naming that field, and nothing is created, decided, versioned or shared.

API surface
An unknown path under /api/ answers a JSON 404 and a published path with an unpublished method answers a JSON 405 with an Allow header listing that path's published methods.

Sign-in lockout
Five refused sign-ins for one work address in its folded form within the window lock that address for the lockout period with an identical 429 and Retry-After, whether the address is known, unknown or deactivated.

Exact first state
A freshly seeded desk holds exactly the published people, realm accounts, requests, attendance rows, leave rows, one policy version, six chained trail entries, no shared links and no sign-in attempts.

Queue state in the URL
The queue's filters, search, sort and page live in a canonical query string carried through row selection, the Desk breadcrumb, reload and Back.

One raise per send
A repeated send by the same person with the same Idempotency-Key and the same values answers 200 with the request as it now stands and Idempotent-Replayed: true, creating nothing, and simultaneous raises for one day create exactly one request.

Business time
Every day the desk stores, filters, counts or checks is a Kestrel Works business date in Europe/London, claimed and shown times are business wall-clock times, and API timestamps are the matching UTC instants.

Daylight-saving claims
A claimed time that does not occur on its business day is refused with 422 naming the field, a time that occurs twice takes the earlier instant, and claims are compared with recorded punches as instants.

Return after sign-in
After signing in, a person lands on the page named by a safe next, and an unsafe next is ignored and never echoed, landing them on /requests.

Hostile values
Malformed or overflowing request ids answer the unknown-id 404, NUL characters and malformed or over-deep JSON answer their named 400, and no answer ever carries a stack, SQL or driver message.

Stable paging
Every queue order is total, so walking every page under any sort yields each matched request exactly once, and a malformed page value is refused with 400.

Focus round trip
The state chips move with arrows, Home and End, opening a request focuses its pane heading, and returning through Desk or Back focuses the originating row's link, as qualified in Interactions.

Policy precondition
A policy save must send If-Match with the version in force, answering 428 when it is missing and 412 when it is stale, so of simultaneous saves on one version exactly one lands and version numbers stay contiguous.

Policy announcements
Saving policy is announced politely while in flight, then the new version or the refusal assertively, a refused field is marked invalid, described by the refusal and focused, and the footer shows the new version without a reload.

Live calendar counts
Calendar counts are read live and move on the corrected business day as soon as a report raises, is approved or withdraws, and each person's waiting total for a month equals that person's pending queue count for the month.

Leave blocks a raise
A raise for a day on which the raiser has approved leave is refused with 422 at its published step, while pending leave does not block.

One seeder
Two desk instances started together against one empty database produce the exact first state once, with a single seeded_on, and both become ready without a server error.

Late realm
A desk started while the realm is unreachable serves /login, answers sign-in with the 503 wording, and lets people sign in within 15 seconds of the realm returning, with no restart.

Session expiry
A session ends once SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS pass without use or SESSION_MAX_SECONDS pass since sign-in, and the next call answers 401 with the ended-session wording while the next page sends the person through sign-in back to itself.

Sickness shown as absence
A manager reading a report's request sees a sickness leave day only as absence in every answer body, page and script, while the raiser and people operations see the true kind.

Live reporting lines
Role, reporting line and active flag are read from the person rows on every call, so a change made by the HR system of record applies on the next call and a deactivated person's open session ends.

Conflict settles on the winner
Nothing in the queue or pane changes state before the server answers, and a decision or withdrawal answered with 409 re-reads and shows the winner's real state beside the 409 wording, without a page load.

Policy save after a colleague
After a 412 the policy form keeps every typed value, names the version that landed and who saved it, and the next save knowingly appends the version after it.

Forced colours
Calendar marks, out-of-month days, focus rings, the selected row edge and state chips stay distinguishable by shape and word, including under a forced-colours setting.

Shared month links
A manager for a current direct report, or people operations for any active person, mints a read-only month link whose token answers 200 while live, 410 once expired, revoked, replaced or out of the minter's scope, 404 when unknown and 403 to any write, with mints throttled per minter, as qualified in Business rules.

Session rotation and folded addresses
Every sign-in issues a new session identifier and ends the session the request presented, and work addresses match for sign-in, uniqueness and lockout in their folded form while a look-alike from another script gets the identical refusal.

Private fields and input limits
A person's phone and private note reach only people operations' request detail and no other answer, page, script, shared month or export, a reason is limited to 280 grapheme clusters with 281 refused 422 naming reason, and a body over 65,536 bytes answers 413.

Trail export and chain
People operations downloads the trail as CSV with formula-leading cells neutralised before quoting and the published framing, and every entry carries a stored hash chain that GET /api/trail/verify checks, naming the lowest broken entry.
/app/run.json is a JSON object with string install, build and serve commands and _schema run-manifest-v1.
/app/USER_README.md lists every seeded work address beside the shared password deku-demo-pw-2026.
The reserved .browser_screenshots/ and .downloads/ directories at /app exist and stay empty.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package with its version and licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package is licensed under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
Shipped packages include exactly one postgres driver and no other database, cache, queue or mail client.
Never download, install or start a copy of postgres or Keycloak, and never change the provided realm's or client's settings.
